newsitem.title: USA: Arraignment of former ADM executives postponed.
newsitem.headline: Arraignment of former ADM executives postponed.

text.p: The arraignment of three former Archer Daniels Midland Co. executives who face price-fixing charges was postponed Monday after federal prosecutors failed to get the case assigned to a different judge.

First Assistant U.S. Attorney Scott Lassar said U.S. District Judge Blanche Manning will preside over the case against Michael Andreas, who recently took leave as vice chairman of ADM; Terrance Wilson, a former group vice president in charge of corn refining; and Mark Whitacre, who had headed ADM's BioProducts Division.
The three were charged with allegedly fixing prices of lysine, a feed additive.
The case was assigned originally to Manning, but prosecutors had attempted to have it transferred to Judge Ruben Castillo.

Castillo presided over Decatur, Ill.-based ADM's antitrust case, in which the company pleaded guilty to two counts of fixing prices of lysine and citric acid, a food and feed additive. ADM also agreed to pay a record $100 million in fines.
As of midday Monday, no date had been set for the arraignments.
Michael Andreas is the son of ADM Chairman Dwayne Andreas.
Whitacre acted as an informant for more than three years as part of the Justice Department's investigation of alleged price-fixing in the feed and food additives industries.
He was fired from Decatur, Ill.-based ADM in August 1995 after the company alleged he stole $9.0 million from it. Whitacre has denied those charges.
Earlier this month, Whitacre said he was no longer cooperating with the government in its price-fixing case.
